A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of cryoballoon ablation for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in patients with atrial fibrillation is safe and effective.

the standard biomarkers of myocardial injury, such as troponin I and T, CK, CK-MB, and LDH, are useful for the early detection of myocardial injury in patients undergoing pulmonary vein isolation with a cryoballoon.

we have shown that the use of cryoballooning for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is associated with a low rate of myocardial injury, and the use of standard biomarkers is not useful to identify patients with myocardial injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a cryoballoon for pulmonary vein isolation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is associated with an increase in cardiac troponin I (cTnI) levels and that these increases are not predictive of myocardial damage.

the use of the cryoablation catheter for pulmonary vein isolation is associated with an increased risk of atrial fibrillation (AF), and the use of the radiofrequency ablation catheter is associated with an increase in stroke.
the current biomarkers for cardiac injury (troponins and CK-MB) are not sensitive enough to detect myocardial injury after PVI with a cryoballoon.
